trust_decision.summary: Caller-supplied FormData field-name path parts are used unchecked as property keys on the result object; the only point that decides which keys may be read/assigned is handlePathPart's object branch (fix adds a forbidden-key check there).

landing_point.why: Summary says __proto__ in field names; the only bracket-property get/set on a caller key in the object branch of handlePathPart is here, and the file is ~500 lines.

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: Only one implementation; array branch (src/index.ts:346-364) cannot receive non-digit keys because the regex restricts array segments to \d* (src/index.ts:266). Custom transformEntry (src/index.ts:469) feeds the same path parser, not a separate sink.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: A solver could argue the array branch or custom transformEntry paths are out of scope, but neither reaches a distinct sink; there is no real route to dismiss.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Ordinary nested keys that resemble forbidden ones (e.g. 'proto', '__proto__x', 'constructorName', 'a.b') and array/object nesting must keep producing plain objects; a fix switching result to Object.create(null) or rejecting by substring would change output or break those.

O6_input_shapes: a[__proto__] (array-bracket form, rejected via regex/duplicate guard)

O7_producer.where: extractPathParts (src/index.ts:265-294) produces the path parts; it is a parser feeding the same check, not a separate producer layer

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Loosen array segment regex to accept named indices (a[key]) so the array branch writes currentArray[key] without the object-branch check.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Supporting PHP/qs-style a[key] bracket notation is a common feature request; the fix's own test comment (fix.diff:167-173) anticipates exactly this.

O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: A 'defaults'/'initialValues' option is a plausible form-library addition, and deep-merge helpers are a classic second pollution sink in another function.
